Counterfactual half of Ban--Kédagni aggregate bounded-support equality
Same-direction correlation, optionally strengthened by less endogeneity

definitions.name: \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Q^r(P)=\{Q:Q_{Y,D,Z}=P,\ Q(Y=Y_D)=1,\ \operatorname{Supp}_P(Y\mid D=a)=\operatorname{Supp}_Q(Y_a\mid D\ne a)=[\ell_a,u_a],\ \Psi_r(Q,a)=1\text{ for every }a\in\{d,e\},\text{ and }r=\mathrm{LEI}\Rightarrow\sigma_Z>0\}\)

definitions.name: \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)\)
definitions.construction: \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)=\max_{x_a,t_a}\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}t_{a,j}\) subject to \(x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\) and \(0\le t_{a,j}\le x_{a,j}-\ell_a\), \(t_{a,j}\le u_a-x_{a,j}\) for every \(j\in\mathcal M_a\), with value \(-\infty\) when \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)=\varnothing\)

definitions.name: \(P^\star\)
definitions.construction: Under \(P^\star\), \((D,Z)\) takes \((0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\) with probabilities \((2/25,9/20,9/25,11/100)\); \(Y\mid(D,Z)=(0,z)\) is uniform on \([0,1]\), \(Y\mid(D,Z)=(1,0)\) is \(\operatorname{Beta}(79,21)\), and \(Y\mid(D,Z)=(1,1)\) is \(\operatorname{Beta}(17,3)\)

definitions.name: \(\mathcal I_{BK}^\star\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal I_{BK}^\star=[0.496024,0.872824]\), the union obtained by evaluating the normalized multiplier formulas of BanKedagni2022 at \(P^\star\) for arm \(a=1\)

definitions.name: \((P_\varepsilon)_{|\varepsilon|<3/110}\)
definitions.construction: Under \(P_\varepsilon\), \((D,Z)\) has masses \((1/2,1/4,1/4)\) at \((0,0),(1,0),(1,2)\); the first cell outcome is uniform on \([0,1]\), the second is \(\operatorname{Beta}(9,1)\), and the third has density \(f_\varepsilon(y)=f_0(y)[1+\varepsilon(y-3/10)/(21/1100)]\) on \([0,1]\), where \(f_0\) is the \(\operatorname{Beta}(3,7)\) density

definitions.name: \(\mathcal I_{\partial,q}(P_\varepsilon)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal I_{\partial,q}(P_\varepsilon)=\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_\varepsilon)\) when \(q=\mathrm{arm}\), and \(\mathcal I_{\partial,q}(P_\varepsilon)=\mathcal I_{\Delta}^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P_\varepsilon)\) with \((d,e)=(1,0)\) when \(q=\mathrm{ATE}\)

definitions.name: \(\mathcal H_n\)
definitions.construction: On the binary-treatment inference submodel \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\), whose fixed grid therefore satisfies \(d_j\in\{d,e\}\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\), define \(\mathcal H_n=\{(p,\omega):p=(\pi_j)_{j\in\mathcal J},\ \omega=(\omega_j)_{j\in\mathcal J},\ \pi_j\ge0,\ \sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\pi_j=1,\ 0\le\omega_j\le\pi_j,\ |\pi_j-\widehat p_j|\le\eta_n,\ |\omega_j-\widehat\omega_j|\le\eta_n\text{ for every }j\in\mathcal J\}\)

definitions.name: \(p(P')\) and \(\omega(P')\)
definitions.construction: On the binary-treatment inference submodel \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\), every candidate law \(P'\) has \(P'\{D\in\{d,e\}\}=1\). Define \(p(P')=(p_j(P'))_{j\in\mathcal J}\) and \(\omega(P')=(\omega_j(P'))_{j\in\mathcal J}\) by \(p_j(P')=P'\{(D,Z)=c_j\}\) and \(\omega_j(P')=\mathbb E_{P'}[\mathbf 1\{(D,Z)=c_j\}(Y-\ell_{d_j})/(u_{d_j}-\ell_{d_j})]\). Because \(d_j\in\{d,e\}\) and \(Y\in[\ell_{D},u_D]\) almost surely, these are unconditional bounded moments satisfying \(0\le\omega_j(P')\le p_j(P')\); they require no conditional-mean division.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak D_+^r\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak D_+^r=\{(p,\omega):p=(\pi_j)_{j\in\mathcal J},\ \omega=(\omega_j)_{j\in\mathcal J},\ \pi_j>0,\ 0\le\omega_j\le\pi_j\text{ for every }j,\ \sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\pi_j=1,\text{ and }r=\mathrm{LEI}\Rightarrow\sum_j\pi_j(d_j-\sum_k\pi_kd_k)^2>0\text{ and }\sum_j\pi_j(z_j-\sum_k\pi_kz_k)^2>0\}\)

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak I_a^r(p,\omega)\) and \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta}^r(p,\omega)\)
definitions.construction: For \((p,\omega)\in\mathfrak D_+^r\), set \(m_j(p,\omega)=\ell_{d_j}+(u_{d_j}-\ell_{d_j})\omega_j/\pi_j\), \(\mu_D(p)=\sum_j\pi_jd_j\), \(\mu_Z(p)=\sum_j\pi_jz_j\), \(\sigma_D(p)^2=\sum_j\pi_j(d_j-\mu_D(p))^2\), and \(\sigma_Z(p)^2=\sum_j\pi_j(z_j-\mu_Z(p))^2\). Define \(s_j^{\mathrm{SDC}}(p)=(d_j-\mu_D(p),z_j-\mu_Z(p))'\) and \(s_j^{\mathrm{LEI}}(p)=((z_j-\mu_Z(p))/\sigma_Z(p),(d_j-\mu_D(p))/\sigma_D(p)-(z_j-\mu_Z(p))/\sigma_Z(p))'\). For each arm and branch, set \(c_a(p,\omega)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal O_a}\pi_jm_j(p,\omega)\), \(h_a^r(p,\omega)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal O_a}\pi_js_j^r(p)m_j(p,\omega)\), and \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(p,\omega)=\{x_a\in\prod_{j\in\mathcal M_a}[\ell_a,u_a]:b(h_a^r(p,\omega)+\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}\pi_js_j^r(p)x_{a,j})\ge0\text{ coordinatewise}\}\). Let \(\tau_{a,b}^r(p,\omega)\) be the maximum of \(\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}t_{a,j}\) over this polytope subject to \(0\le t_{a,j}\le x_{a,j}-\ell_a\) and \(t_{a,j}\le u_a-x_{a,j}\), with value \(-\infty\) for an empty polytope, and set \(\mathcal B_a^r(p,\omega)=\{b:\tau_{a,b}^r(p,\omega)>0\}\). Define \(L_{a,b}^r(p,\omega)\) and \(U_{a,b}^r(p,\omega)\) as the minimum and maximum of \(c_a(p,\omega)+\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}\pi_jx_{a,j}\) over \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(p,\omega)\). Finally, \(\mathfrak I_a^r(p,\omega)=\bigcup_{b\in\mathcal B_a^r(p,\omega)}[L_{a,b}^r(p,\omega),U_{a,b}^r(p,\omega)]\) and \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta}^r(p,\omega)=\bigcup_{b\in\mathcal B_d^r(p,\omega),\,h\in\mathcal B_e^r(p,\omega)}[L_{d,b}^r(p,\omega)-U_{e,h}^r(p,\omega),U_{d,b}^r(p,\omega)-L_{e,h}^r(p,\omega)]\). Both maps depend only on the primitive pair and fixed grid, and no ratio is formed outside the domain \(\pi_j>0\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal C_n\)
definitions.construction: On the binary-treatment inference submodel \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\), \(\mathcal C_n=\operatorname{cl}\bigcup\{\mathfrak I_{\Delta}^r(p,\omega):(p,\omega)\in\mathcal H_n\cap\mathfrak D_+^r\}\), with the analogous primitive-map construction for either reported arm mean. Candidate pairs with a zero cell mass are outside \(\mathfrak D_+^r\), so this image never evaluates \(m_j(p,\omega)\) at \(\pi_j=0\).

definitions.name: \(\mathsf A_{\mathrm{arr}}\)
definitions.construction: Enumerate the origin and every nonnegative intersection of two linearly independent members of \(\{\lambda_1=0,\lambda_2=0,1-b\lambda's_j^r=0:j\in\mathcal M_a\}\), evaluate the relevant piecewise-affine cone dual at those points, and attach a separate primal feasibility or recession certificate

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\)
definitions.construction: On the binary-treatment inference submodel \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\), begin with \(\mathcal H_n\), stratify candidate laws by the LP-computed slack \(\tau_{a,b}^r\), and invert a studentized test of the primitive mass vector on each slack stratum; the data-dependent critical value and final region are to be derived

statements.statement: For either \(r=\mathrm{SDC}\) or \(r=\mathrm{LEI}\), every \(Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\) induces, for each arm \(a\), a sign \(b\in\{-1,+1\}\) and missing-cell means \(x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\) such that \(\theta_a(Q)=c_a+\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_jx_{a,j}\). Conversely, every vector in \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\) is realized by a bounded missing-cell completion satisfying the branch score inequalities; exact aggregate support is addressed by Theorem 1.
statements.justification: This is the finite-dimensional reduction that separates moment feasibility from full-support completion.
statements.gap: BanKedagni2022 derives valid inequalities but does not identify the missing-cell completion polytope or prove a converse.
statements.consumer: Every later endpoint, support, and computation result reduces to this finite object.

statements.statement: Fix \(a\in\{d,e\}\), \(b\in\{-1,+1\}\), and \(r\in\mathcal R\). The branch admits a completion satisfying the exact aggregate support equality if and only if \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)>0\). Equivalently, \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\) contains a vector with at least one coordinate strictly between \(\ell_a\) and \(u_a\), or, equivalently, it is not a singleton box vertex. For every eligible branch, the closure of exact-support arm means is \([L_{a,b}^r(P),U_{a,b}^r(P)]\), and hence the full closure equals \(\mathcal I_a^r(P)\).
statements.justification: The strict slack is the exact branch filter created by aggregate support equality.
statements.gap: The published bounded-support formulas do not distinguish an algebraically feasible box-vertex branch from a branch admitting full interval support. KédagniLiMourifie2018 Theorem 1 proves sharpness under rectangular support and finite zero-covariance equalities, but it does not characterize which SDC inequality branch admits exact aggregate-support completion; in the shared binary specialization \(g(y)=y\) and \(h(Z)=Z\), its zero-covariance class is contained in the SDC class considered here.
statements.consumer: The filter changes the reported imperfect-IV region in the Ban--Kédagni NLSYM and Yu air-pollution workflows whenever a fitted branch has zero slack.

statements.statement: For every nonempty branch \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\), finite linear-program duality gives \(L_{a,b}^r(P)=V_{L,a,b}^r(P)\) and \(U_{a,b}^r(P)=V_{U,a,b}^r(P)\), with attaining unrestricted multipliers in \(\mathbb R_+^2\). Combined with Theorem 1, these values give the sharp exact-support arm-mean closure. At \(P^\star\) for \(a=1\) and \(r=\mathrm{SDC}\), \(\mathcal I_1^{\mathrm{SDC}}(P^\star)=[711/1100,911/1100]\subsetneq\mathcal I_{BK}^\star=[0.496024,0.872824]\), so the theorem strictly tightens the published normalized outer union at a legal full-support law.
statements.justification: The unrestricted cone is the intrinsic LP dual, and the rational example makes the correction empirically nonvacuous.
statements.gap: BanKedagni2022 normalizes the multiplier magnitude and states validity without sharpness; earlier cone discussion does not supply endpoint duality or the support filter. KédagniLiMourifie2018 Theorem 2 gives an equivalent unit-sphere characterization for its finite zero-covariance model, whereas this theorem dualizes the two-inequality SDC sign cone and combines it with the positive-slack support filter; for arbitrary finite \(h\), the two moment classes overlap but are not generally nested.
statements.consumer: Applied users obtain exact population endpoints and a certificate showing when the published outer region is unnecessarily wide.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\ne\varnothing\) and no restriction beyond membership in \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\) couples distinct potential-outcome arms. Conditional product coupling of separately chosen arm kernels preserves the observed factual law, every armwise score restriction, and every aggregate support. Therefore the sharp ATE closure for \(\Delta_{d,e}\) is exactly \(\mathcal I_{\Delta}^r(P)\).
statements.justification: Marginal sharpness does not by itself establish that two arms attain opposite endpoints on one full-data law.
statements.gap: Park2025 proves joint attainment under MIV plus MTR; no checked result supplies the conditional product witness under armwise SDC and exact aggregate support.
statements.consumer: The proposition justifies reporting ATE differences of eligible arm intervals rather than an unverified subtraction of marginal outer bounds.

statements.statement: For \(P^\star\), the four SDC branch endpoint certificates are \((x,y)=(0,29531/49500)\), \((0,200287/211500)\), \((1,54229/70500)\), and \((1,40731/49500)\). Each vector has an interior coordinate, and cone multipliers \((0,25/11)\) certify the outer sharp endpoints; these multipliers lie outside the published normalized simplex.
statements.justification: Exact rational certificates prevent the strict comparison from resting on floating-point optimization.
statements.gap: No published example isolates a legal aggregate-support SDC law at which normalization loses both sharp outer endpoints.
statements.consumer: The certificates form a reproducible regression test for any implementation of the sharp-set algorithm.

statements.statement: Along \((P_\varepsilon)\) under SDC, the arm-\(1\) closure is \([3/5,4/5]\) at \(\varepsilon=0\) and \([3/10+\varepsilon/4,3/10+\varepsilon]\cup[3/5+\varepsilon/2,4/5+\varepsilon/4]\) for \(0<\varepsilon<3/110\). The arm-\(0\) closure is \([1/4,3/4]\), so the ATE closures are \([-3/20,11/20]\) at zero and \([-9/20+\varepsilon/4,11/20+\varepsilon/4]\) for positive \(\varepsilon\). Both set maps are Hausdorff-discontinuous at zero. For every \(q\in\{\mathrm{arm},\mathrm{ATE}\}\) and every positive \(\varepsilon_n=o(1/n)\), \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat I_n}\max_{P\in\{P_0,P_{\varepsilon_n}\}}\mathbb E_{P^n}[\rho_H(\widehat I_n,\mathcal I_{\partial,q}(P))]\ge3/20\), where the infimum is over measurable nonempty compact-set estimators. This claim is SDC-only and makes no LEI boundary assertion.
statements.justification: The theorem exposes the statistical cost of treating exact support eligibility as a discontinuous branch decision.
statements.gap: Generic LP nonregularity is known, but the cited literature does not give this legal SDC family, the exact set jump, or the \(3/20\) minimax constant.
statements.consumer: Inference procedures for the exact set can be screened against an explicit impossibility benchmark instead of promising uniform shrinking at zero slack.

statements.statement: Restrict the inference result to the binary-treatment submodel \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P^r\) satisfying \(P\{D\in\{d,e\}\}=1\), the primitive moment map satisfies \((p(P),\omega(P))\in\mathfrak D_+^r\), \(\mathfrak I_a^r(p(P),\omega(P))=\mathcal I_a^r(P)\) for \(a\in\{d,e\}\), and \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta}^r(p(P),\omega(P))=\mathcal I_{\Delta}^r(P)\). Under the fixed known binary-treatment grid and ranges, \(\Pr_P\{(p(P),\omega(P))\in\mathcal H_n\}\ge1-\alpha\), and therefore \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P^r:\,P\{D\in\{d,e\}\}=1}\Pr_P\{\mathcal I_{\Delta}^r(P)\subseteq\mathcal C_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(n\). Replacing the ATE image by either \(\mathfrak I_a^r\) image gives simultaneous coverage of both target-arm closures on the same event. Coverage holds at \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)=0\) because projection precedes application of the exact-set map; zero-mass candidate cells are excluded without excluding the strictly positive population pair fixed by \(\mathcal J=\operatorname{Supp}_P(D,Z)\).
statements.justification: Projection of the explicit primitive-moment image preserves finite-sample honesty despite branch discontinuity.
statements.gap: BanKedagni2022 treats intersection-bound outer formulas, while calibrated projection and perturbed-LP methods do not directly cover a support-filtered union whose components disappear.
statements.consumer: NLSYM-style and air-pollution analyses can report a conservative confidence region for the entire exact population set, including a zero-slack diagnostic.

statements.statement: For either two-score mode and every feasible branch, \(\mathsf A_{\mathrm{arr}}\) returns the same endpoint as the primal LP and the unrestricted cone dual after \(O(|\mathcal M_a|^2)\) candidate intersections and \(O(|\mathcal M_a|^3)\) naive arithmetic per endpoint. A separate LP computes \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)\); primal infeasibility or a dual recession ray certifies an empty branch. The statement includes parallel kink lines, zero scores, tied optima, and structural-zero cells removed before forming \(\mathcal J\).
statements.justification: Exact branch and endpoint certificates are essential near the zero-slack boundary.
statements.gap: Generic LP solvers compute values but do not expose this two-score finite certificate or prevent finite-multiplier confusion with infeasibility.
statements.consumer: A production implementation can certify the early-kill cases \(\varepsilon=-0.001,0,0.001\) without ad hoc tolerances changing the population target.

statements.statement: If exact aggregate support equality is replaced by the standard bounded-range condition \(Y_a\in[\ell_a,u_a]\), every nonempty branch contributes its full attained interval regardless of \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)\). If the score restrictions are also removed, the branch polytope is the full box and the resulting arm endpoints are the classical Manski worst-case bounds.
statements.justification: The reduction verifies that the support filter, rather than bounded outcomes alone, causes branch pruning.
statements.gap: This is a required sanity reduction, not a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Readers can distinguish the exact-support contribution from standard worst-case bounded-outcome identification.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\), can one construct a computable region \(\widetilde{\mathcal C}_n\) that is uniformly honest for \(\mathcal I_{\Delta}^r(P)\) over the binary-treatment fixed-grid model \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\), contracts at the regular LP-value rate uniformly on every class with \(\min_{a,b:\tau_{a,b}^r(P)>0}\tau_{a,b}^r(P)\ge\kappa_n\), and attains a matching lower frontier as \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\), while reverting to the nonshrinking behavior required by Theorem 3 at the boundary?
statements.justification: The open content is an honest adaptation frontier between stable positive slack and disappearing branches.
statements.gap: ChoRussell2024, KaidoMolinariStoye2019, and BaiEtAl2026 do not derive a completion-slack-indexed rate frontier for this exact-set map.
statements.consumer: Such a region would replace the conservative projection region away from branch boundaries without contradicting the minimax impossibility at zero slack.

sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed sampling from the observed law \(P\)
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(Y_i,D_i,Z_i)\) on a fixed finite positive-mass cell grid; the finite-sample projection theorem uses the binary-treatment submodel
sampling_model.treatment: The structural identification results allow finite-valued \(D_i\) with target arms \(d\) and \(e\); the sampling and inference construction restricts \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\)
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cell masses and bounded outcome masses are empirical averages; conditional means are derived only inside the positive-mass primitive map

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under bounded support and SDC, Proposition 3.1 gives nonparametric bounds for \(\theta_d\) as a normalized union.

Theorems 1--2 give sharp product-form arm-mean and ATE bounds and an equivalent unit-sphere inequality characterization under rectangular bounded supports and finitely many unconditional zero-covariance restrictions.
Same-direction and less-endogenous correlations bound a constant effect in a parametric linear model.
Proposition 1 gives sharp arm-mean and ATE bounds under MIV plus MTR.
Theorem 3.1 establishes uniformly valid calibrated projection for fixed finite moment models.
The procedure bootstraps value functions of randomly perturbed linear programs.
Ordinary bootstrap consistency requires full differentiability when the first-stage limit is Gaussian.
The paper characterizes total-variation closure before testing linear systems with unknown coefficients.
The paper tests whether estimated linear equality and inequality constraints admit a solution.
Theorem 2 gives robust inference for nonsmooth covariate-assisted valid-IV bounds under a margin condition.
The paper develops estimation and inference for intersection bounds.

tldr: For finite imperfect-instrument cells, SDC and SDC-plus-LEI reduce to a union of bounded missing-cell completion polytopes. Ban--Kédagni aggregate support equality retains exactly the branches with positive maximum interior slack. Unrestricted cone duals then give sharp arm-mean closures, and conditional product coupling gives the sharp ATE closure. A rational four-cell law produces \([711/1100,911/1100]\), strictly inside the published normalized outer union. A legal three-cell SDC family shows a Hausdorff jump and a \(3/20\) two-point minimax loss, while, on the binary-treatment submodel, simultaneous Hoeffding projection over primitive moments covers the entire exact set in finite samples.

project_justification.gap: Ban and Kédagni impose exact aggregate support equality but derive normalized valid bounds and explicitly leave sharpness unresolved. Their formulas do not decide whether an algebraically feasible sign branch admits the required full support.
project_justification.niche: Finite-cell SDC geometry permits an exact separation between correlation-cone feasibility, aggregate-support eligibility, endpoint optimization, and cross-arm coupling. The separation also reveals a discontinuous branch boundary that fixed-system LP inference does not describe.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the positive-slack eligibility equivalence, unrestricted-cone sharp endpoints, simultaneous ATE completion, exact strict and discontinuity examples, a quantitative minimax boundary result, and a conservative finite-sample whole-set confidence region.

related_work: Ban and Kédagni (2022) provide the exact support assumption and valid normalized SDC and SDC-plus-LEI outer formulas; Theorem 2 strictly tightens their SDC union at \(P^\star\). Kédagni, Li, and Mourifié (2018, public non-archival working paper) give sharp bounds under finitely many unconditional zero-covariance equalities: their Theorem 1 establishes the sharp Cartesian-product arm-mean set and its ATE implication, while their Theorem 2 gives the equivalent unit-sphere moment-inequality characterization without centering normalization. On binary treatment with \(g(y)=y\), their rectangular-support condition coincides with the aggregate-support equality here; when \(h(Z)=Z\), their zero-covariance class is contained in the proposal's SDC class because \(\operatorname{Cov}(Y_a,Z)=0\) implies SDC, but SDC also permits nonzero instrument covariance. For arbitrary finite transformations \(h\), their equality class and the SDC class generally overlap without either containing the other. Accordingly, Theorem 1 supplies the branchwise positive-slack eligibility criterion absent from their Theorem 1, and Theorem 2 supplies endpoint duality for the SDC sign cone rather than claiming to subsume their general moment class. Nevo and Rosen (2012) supply the parametric interpretation of same-direction and less-endogenous correlations. Park (2025) informs the joint-attainment step under a different MIV-plus-MTR model and is not a tightening target. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), Cho and Russell (2024), and Fang and Santos (2019) inform projection, perturbed-LP, and directional-derivative methods, respectively. Bai et al. (2026) and Goff and Mbakop (2026) establish generic linear-system closure and testing results, so generic nonregularity is not claimed here. Levis et al. (2025) informs the open adaptive-inference question through its margin-based treatment of nonsmooth conditional bounds. Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013) remains the comparator for the published intersection-bound inference workflow, not for the exact support-filtered set.
technical_internal_limitation: Exact decisions at \(\tau_{a,b}^r(P)=0\) require rational arithmetic, interval certificates, or explicit primal--dual tolerances that preserve the mathematical target. The coverage construction is conservative, is restricted to binary treatment, and may require global optimization over positive-mass candidate primitive pairs. The fixed grid, known support endpoints, and independent sampling are maintained. The three-cell discontinuity theorem is SDC-only; it does not establish an LEI boundary. Covariate adjustment, clustered sampling, estimated supports, empirical re-estimation, and unrestricted contraction are outside scope.
honest_scope: The theorem-level kernel is the exact support filter plus sharp cone endpoints and joint arm completion. The rational four-cell and three-cell claims are population statements, not empirical findings. The finite-sample projection theorem and boundary-adaptive inference question are restricted to the binary-treatment submodel \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\). Removing exact support recovers the standard bounded-range completion problem, and removing the score restrictions recovers Manski worst-case bounds. Boundary-adaptive shrinking with an optimal slack-indexed frontier remains the explicit open-ended question.

literature_map.anchor_read: BanKedagni2022 introduces invalid instruments through interpretable correlation restrictions, states exact factual--counterfactual interval-support equality in Assumption 2.1, derives normalized outer bounds in Proposition 3.1, and explicitly leaves sharpness unproved; its conclusion returns to computable ATE regions and the NLSYM application.
adjacent_threads: KedagniLiMourifie2018 Theorems 1--2 prove sharp product-form arm and ATE bounds and an equivalent unit-sphere characterization under rectangular support and finitely many unconditional zero-covariance equalities; for binary treatment and \(h(Z)=Z\), that equality class is contained in the present SDC class, while arbitrary finite transformations produce overlapping but generally nonnested moment classes.
NevoRosen2012 supplies the parametric SDC and LEI origin but not heterogeneous-outcome completion.
Park2025 proves sharp arm and ATE bounds under the structurally different MIV-plus-MTR model and motivates an explicit joint attainment construction.
ChoRussell2024 treats perturbed value functions for fixed linear programs, while the exact-support filter changes which programs contribute.
BaiEtAl2026 and GoffMbakop2026 treat closure and testing for generic linear systems with estimated coefficients, not aggregate-support eligibility.
literature_map.occupancy_conclusion: No checked paper supplies the equivalence \(\tau_{a,b}^r>0\) for exact aggregate support, the unrestricted cone endpoint formula, and a simultaneous SDC or SDC-plus-LEI arm completion.

literature_map.anchor_read: KaidoMolinariStoye2019 proves uniformly valid calibrated projection for fixed finite moment systems under local geometric regularity; its conclusion emphasizes projection coverage and repeated feasibility optimization.
adjacent_threads: FangSantos2019 proves ordinary-bootstrap failure for merely directionally differentiable maps and motivates derivative-aware resampling.
ChoRussell2024 obtains uniform inference by random perturbation of LP values under genericity.
BaiEtAl2026 characterizes total-variation closure obstructions for unknown-coefficient linear systems.
literature_map.occupancy_conclusion: Generic nonregularity is occupied, but the explicit SDC branch-disappearance family, exact \(3/20\) Hausdorff-risk lower bound, and primitive-moment whole-set projection are not subsumed.

novelty_justification: The closest published result is Ban and Kédagni's Proposition 3.1, which gives valid normalized intersection bounds and explicitly says that sharpness is unproved. The proposed kernel replaces that outer calculation by an exact missing-cell completion problem: a sign branch contributes under their aggregate-support equality if and only if its maximum total interior slack is positive. Unrestricted nonnegative-cone duality then yields sharp arm-mean closures, and conditional product coupling yields the sharp ATE closure. Kédagni, Li, and Mourifié's public non-archival Theorems 1--2 establish sharpness for finite unconditional zero-covariance equalities under rectangular support, not for the SDC inequality union or its branch-interiority filter; their \(h(Z)=Z\) binary-treatment specialization is contained in SDC, while arbitrary finite \(h\) yields an overlapping, generally nonnested class. Park's sharp MIV-plus-MTR result uses order restrictions and does not imply this completion criterion. Generic LP-inference and linear-system papers explain some computational and testing tools, but none supplies the aggregate-support filter or the stated imperfect-IV sharp set.
